questions.enonce_markdown: Find the range of values of $x$ which satisfy the inequality $x^2 - 5x + 4 \le 0$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Factorise: $x^2 - 5x + 4 = (x-1)(x-4)$, so we need $(x-1)(x-4) \le 0$.

The roots are $x = 1$ and $x = 4$. The parabola $y = x^2 - 5x + 4$ opens upwards, so it is below or on the $x$-axis between its roots.

| Interval | $x-1$ | $x-4$ | product |
|---|---|---|---|
| $x < 1$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $1 < x < 4$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $x > 4$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

**Answer: $1 \le x \le 4$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Represent the solution on a number line. *[6 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Draw a number line marked at least from $0$ to $5$. Put a **solid (filled) dot** at $1$ and another at $4$, because the inequality is $\le$ (the end values are included). Draw a thick line (or shade) joining the two dots.

The thick segment covers all values from $1$ to $4$, so it shows $1 \le x \le 4$. *(Figure to be drawn by the candidate.)*
